newsitem.title: JAPAN: TENNIS-GRAF POWERS PAST MAJOLI IN PAN PACIFIC.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF POWERS PAST MAJOLI IN PAN PACIFIC.

text.p: World number one Steffi Graf on Friday continued her rebound from a disastrous week, powering past Croatia's Iva Majoli 6-2 6-3 in a quarterfinal of the Pan Pacific women's open.
The win kept Graf on course for a possible showdown in the final on Sunday with Switzerland's teenage star Martina Hingis, who plays her quarter final later on Friday.
The top-seeded Graf, who last week was knocked out of the Australian Open in the fourth round and then saw her father convicted of tax evasion, finished off fifth seed Majoli in just 55 minutes.
Defending champion Majoli started out well, holding her own with Graf until the sixth game of the first set, when the relentless Graf's power turned the tide in her favour.
"The match had some really good rallies," Graf told reporters. "I'm happy about the match."
Asked to compare herself to the second-seeded Hingis, 16, who is playing in a different part of the draw, Graf, 26, said age was the main difference.
"Obviously 10 years makes a big difference. You're young, there's more excitement, you've got nothing to lose," she said.
"Ten years later, you're a different person. You're not as naive or as open-minded as you were 10 years ago," Graf said.
In Saturday's semifinal, Graf will pay eighth-seeded Brenda Schultz-McCarthy of the Netherlands, who beat Spain's Conchita Martinez 6-1, 6-0.

Hingis needs to overcome Amanda Coetzer of South Africa in her quarterfinal and then will possibly go on to a semifinal showdown with the winner of the quarterfinal between American Lindsay Davenport and Germany's Anke Huber.
